excerpt.rendered: Eagles. Running. Walking. The order in Isaiah 40:31 is deliberate — and it says something profound about every stage of the faith journey. Today’s devotional on renewed strength.

content.rendered:
📖 Scripture

“But those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint.”
— Isaiah 40:31 (NIV)

📝 Message

Notice the order. Eagles. Running. Walking.

Most people expect the progression to go the other way — walk, then run, then soar. Start small, build momentum, eventually reach the heights. But Isaiah reverses it deliberately, and the reversal is instructive.

Faith begins with the extraordinary — soaring on wings like eagles, the sudden breakthrough, the mountaintop moment, the unmistakable move of God. It is exhilarating. It is unforgettable. And then the test of real faith is what comes next: can you run when you cannot soar? Can you keep going in the middle season, when the pace is demanding and the breakthrough has not yet come again?

And then the hardest part of all: can you walk when you cannot run? Can you put one foot in front of the other on the ordinary Tuesday, the unremarkable week, the long stretch of faithful mundane obedience when nothing spectacular is happening and nobody is watching?

The promise is for all three. Not just the eagle moments. Not just the seasons of obvious momentum. God promises that those who hope in Him — who wait on Him, who expectantly trust Him — will have strength renewed for every mode of the journey. The soaring. The running. And the quiet, steady, daily walk.

The word “hope” here is qavah in Hebrew — to wait with expectation, like a rope being twisted and strengthened. Waiting on God is not passive resignation. It is active trust that builds strength in you even as you wait. By the time you need to move, you are stronger than you were.

Whatever mode you are in today — soaring, running or simply walking — His strength is sufficient for it.

🙏 Prayer

Lord, I wait on You today. I confess that I have been trying to generate my own momentum — and I am weary from it. Renew my strength as only You can. Whether this is a season for soaring, for running, or simply for faithful walking — give me exactly the grace I need for the pace You have set. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

I hope in the Lord and my strength is being renewed. I will soar on wings like eagles. I will run and not grow weary. I will walk and not faint. The strength I need for today does not come from my own resources — it comes from the God who never grows tired and never runs out. I draw from His strength now.

📖 Further Reading

  • Isaiah 40:27–31 — Read the full passage on God who does not grow weary
  • Psalm 27:13–14 — Wait for the Lord; be strong and take heart
  • Galatians 6:9 — Let us not grow weary in doing good
  • Hebrews 12:1–3 — Run with endurance the race set before us
  • 2 Corinthians 12:9 — My grace is sufficient for you, my power is made perfect in weakness
  • Psalm 46:1 — God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble
